ChatOKF

The model runs here. Not somewhere else.

A free chat app for the Mac and the iPhone. It answers much like the assistants you have used in a browser, except the part that does the thinking is downloaded onto your own device, so your conversation never leaves it.

01What it is

A chat app that keeps the conversation on your own machine.

ChatOKF is a chat application for the Mac and the iPhone. The difference is where the thinking happens. There is no server behind it, so when you type a question, nothing is uploaded and nothing is logged. The answer is computed by your own hardware, a few centimetres from your hands.

It works on a plane, on a train, in a basement, and on the day the service you were relying on shuts down. Once the model is downloaded, the network is optional.

The same app on both, in whichever theme the system is wearing. Every word on these two screens was produced by the machine it is displayed on.

02What it does

It reads, looks, listens, and shows its work.

  1. 01

    Talk or type

    Ask by keyboard, or tap the microphone and speak. Replies can be read back aloud in a voice that is also synthesized on the device.

  2. 02

    Show it a picture

    Attach a photo and ask about it. Some models take sound and video too, and you can watch the frames go by as it looks.

  3. 03

    Hand it a document

    Drop in a PDF, a Word file, a spreadsheet or a page of notes. It reads the text out of them, tables included, and answers from what is inside.

  4. 04

    Watch it think

    The stronger models reason before answering, and you can read that reasoning, cut it short when you have seen enough, or switch it off for a faster reply.

  5. 05

    Give it tools

    A calculator it can actually use, the clock, the weather, the headlines, Wikipedia and web search. Each one is a switch you control.

  6. 06

    Keep the result

    Answers are typeset properly, mathematics and all. Any conversation can be searched, renamed, shared as a PDF, and recovered from the trash for thirty days.

03Where your words go

Nowhere, unless you flip a switch.

Most assistants send your sentence to a company. ChatOKF has nowhere to send it. The whole model sits in your device's memory and runs on its own chip, so privacy here is not a policy that could be revised. It is the shape of the thing.

No account. No sign-in. No subscription. No analytics and no telemetry.

04Pick a mind

Small and quick, or large and thoughtful.

Several open models are offered, and you choose. A small one answers almost instantly and fits in a phone. A large one is noticeably smarter and wants a Mac with memory to spare. Each is downloaded once and then belongs to you.

Gemma 4, E2B and E4B Sees pictures, hears sound and watches video. phone + Mac
Gemma 4, 12B The same eyes and ears, with more behind them. Mac, 16 GB+
Qwen3.5, 4B and 9B The everyday range. Good with tools and long answers. Mac, 8 and 16 GB
Qwen3.8, 27B The thoughtful one, in a size for each Mac. Mac, 9 GB+
Ternary Bonsai, 1.7B and 27B Answers directly, without reasoning first. phone + Mac

The app only offers what your device can actually hold, so the list you see is shorter than this one and always runnable.

05How fast

Measured against llama.cpp on the same machine.

Tokens per second on a MacBook Air (M3, 24 GB): reading a 512-token prompt, then writing 128 tokens. The second number in each cell is llama.cpp on the same file and the same protocol. The last column is the same model writing with its own draft head, which most of ours carry.

ModelReadWriteWrite, draftedDrafted
Qwen3.5 4B341 / 31627.0 / 23.934.6 / 24.3
Qwen3.5 9B186 / 17915.6 / 14.118.2 / 16.8
Qwen3.8 27B51.0 / 52.46.0 / 5.78.5 / 5.5
Gemma 4 E2B577 / 67949.8 / 53.665.1
Gemma 4 E4B298 / 33626.9 / 25.844.6
Gemma 4 12B116 / 12011.8 / 11.520.7

llama.cpp build b10796 on the pristine files; ours on the same weights with our own vision, audio and draft tensors added. llama.cpp runs no draft head for Gemma, so that cell is ours alone. One cooled run each, 2026-09-07.

And in a pocket, the same protocol in the app itself:

DeviceModelReadWriteWrite, draftedDrafted
iPad mini A17 ProGemma 4 E4B12313.820.6
iPhone 15 ProGemma 4 E4B13413.720.9
iPhone 12 miniGemma 4 E2B9316.2

The 4 GB phones write without the draft head on purpose: its extra weights do not stay resident there, and paging them every step is slower than not drafting.
